sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by impermeable fluorophore-conjugated substrate staining (CA-Alexa488 or BG-Alexa488) on non-permeabilized cells; signaling function not measured in this study.
sites.rationale: ACVR2A is a single-pass transmembrane receptor with its N-terminus extracellular and C-terminus intracellular; the only extracellular terminus is the mature N-terminus beginning at residue 20. The signal peptide spans residues 1-19 (last residue G at position 19), so a tag placed downstream of the signal peptide inserts at position 19|20 (between G and A). L4 explicitly states the tag is N-terminal and downstream of the signal peptide with a 5xGly linker; L6 confirms surface display by impermeable dye staining on non-permeabilized cells. The junction is 119 residues from the TM boundary (residue 139), providing ample space for a short epitope tag. Full-length hACVR2A N-terminally fused with Halo- or SNAP-tags separated by a 5x glycine linker, placed downstream of the signal peptide sequence, expressed in HEK293 cells as part of a BMP/TGFβ receptor library (PMC9837045). Western blot confirmed expected molecular weight shifts (L5). Surface display confirmed by impermeable CA-Alexa488 / BG-Alexa488 staining of non-permeabilized cells (L6).

sources.claim: BMP/TGFβ receptors, including type I receptors (hALK1-ALK6, rALK7, and hALK2-R206H) and type II receptors (hACVR2A, hACVR2B, hBMPR2, and hTGFBR2) were, therefore, N-terminally fused with Halo- or SNAP-tags separated by a 5x glycine linker downstream the signal peptide sequence, to obtain the receptor library shown in Fig. 1c .

To this end, we expressed in COS7 cells [the system used to characterize the lateral diffusion and interactions of TGF-β and BMP receptors; 8, 40, 41-46] ACVR2A, ALK6, ALK3, ALK4, or ALK2 carrying an ED epitope tag (myc or HA).

literature_notes: All ten ledger lines converge on a single physical junction: the N-terminal extracellular face of ACVR2A immediately after signal peptide cleavage (insert_after_residue=19, G|A). L1/L2 (PMC8855587) report myc/HA ED epitope tags confirmed by FRAP; L3-L6 (PMC9837045) and L7-L9 (preprint of same work) report Halo/SNAP N-terminal fusions with 5xGly linker confirmed by impermeable dye staining; L10 (PMC10854824) reports epitope-tagged ACVR2A in patch/FRAP without specifying residue. Two sites are reported because two independent publications independently validated the same junction with different tag types; the myc/HA tags (L1) are particularly relevant as they are closer in size to the target ALFA tag. No internal sites are proposed because no ledger line pins a specific internal extracellular loop residue or named loop. No C-terminal site is proposed because the C-terminus is intracellular (residues 161-513). No function-abrogating or intracellular insertions appear in the ledger.
